title: Pairs bootstrap inference with hcinfer
text: replicate bootstrap draws n rows replacement original data refits OLS resample. Writing estimate replicate r vector refitted coefficients, bootstrap standard error coefficient standard deviation replicate values. boot_pairs() offers three interval types: "percentile" uses empirical quantiles replicates, "basic" (reverse percentile) reflects quantiles original estimate, "normal" uses estimate plus minus normal quantile times bootstrap standard error.

title: Pairs bootstrap inference with hcinfer
code: library(hcinfer)  schools <- PublicSchools schools$income_scaled <- schools$income / 10000 schools$income_scaled_sq <- schools$income_scaled^2  fit <- lm(expenditure ~ income_scaled + income_scaled_sq, data = schools) fit #>  #> Call: #> lm(formula = expenditure ~ income_scaled + income_scaled_sq,  #>     data = schools) #>  #> Coefficients: #>      (Intercept)     income_scaled  income_scaled_sq   #>            832.9           -1834.2            1587.0

title: Comparing HC Estimators
text: covariance inference objects store robust weights leverage values. leverage values depend fitted model, weights depend HC estimator. next figure mirrors empirical display HCbeta paper: adjustment factors plotted leverages HC3, HC4, HC4m, HCbeta.
code: covariances <- purrr::map(methods, \(method) {   vcov_hc(fit, type = method) }) names(covariances) <- methods  diagnostic_comparison <- purrr::imap(covariances, \(cov, method) {   tibble::tibble(     method = method,     max_leverage = max(cov$leverage),     max_weight = max(cov$weights),     median_weight = stats::median(cov$weights)   ) }) diagnostic_comparison <- dplyr::bind_rows(diagnostic_comparison) diagnostic_comparison #> # A tibble: 5 × 4 #>   method max_leverage max_weight median_weight #>   <chr>         <dbl>      <dbl>         <dbl> #> 1 hc0           0.651       1             1    #> 2 hc3           0.651       8.20          1.08 #> 3 hc4           0.651      67.3           1.03 #> 4 hc4m          0.651      13.9           1.05 #> 5 hcbeta        0.651       4.58          1.19 figure_methods <- c("hc3", "hc4", "hc4m", "hcbeta") figure_covariances <- purrr::map(figure_methods, \(method) {   vcov_hc(fit, type = method) }) names(figure_covariances) <- figure_methods  weight_comparison <- purrr::imap(figure_covariances, \(cov, method) {   tibble::tibble(     method = cov$label,     leverage = cov$leverage,     weight = cov$weights,     high_leverage = cov$leverage > 3 * cov$p / cov$n   ) }) |>   dplyr::bind_rows() |>   dplyr::mutate(     method = factor(method, levels = c("HC3", "HC4", "HC4m", "HCbeta"))   )  ggplot2::ggplot(weight_comparison, ggplot2::aes(x = leverage, y = weight)) +   ggplot2::geom_point(     ggplot2::aes(color = high_leverage),     size = 1.8,     alpha = 0.85   ) +   ggplot2::facet_wrap(~method, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +   ggplot2::scale_color_manual(     values = c(`FALSE` = "#2c5f8a", `TRUE` = "#c0392b"),     guide = "none"   ) +   ggplot2::labs(     x = expression(h[t]),     y = expression(g[t])   ) +   ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   ggplot2::theme(     strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),     panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank()   )

title: Pairs bootstrap standard errors and confidence intervals — boot_pairs
text: B bootstrap replicates, sample n row indices drawn replacement 1, ..., n, OLS refitted resampled rows \((y_{}, x_{})\). Writing \(\hat\beta^{*}_{(r)}\) estimate replicate r, bootstrap standard error coefficient j sample standard deviation \(\hat\beta^{*}_{1,j}, \ldots, \hat\beta^{*}_{B,j}\). Three interval types available ci_type. Let \(q_\alpha\) denote empirical \(\alpha\) quantile bootstrap replicates coefficient, \(\hat\beta_j\) original estimate, \(s^{*}_j\) bootstrap standard error, \(\alpha = 1 - \texttt{level}\). "percentile" interval \([q_{\alpha/2}, q_{1-\alpha/2}]\). "basic" (reverse percentile) interval \([2\hat\beta_j - q_{1-\alpha/2}, \; 2\hat\beta_j - q_{\alpha/2}]\). "normal" interval \(\hat\beta_j \pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\, s^{*}_j\), \(z\) standard normal quantile. Reproducibility. seed supplied, resampling indices drawn , sequentially, main process seed, per-replicate fit deterministic. results therefore identical whether run sequential parallel regardless number cores. caller's random number generator state saved restored, calling boot_pairs() disturb surrounding random stream. seed NULL, current RNG state used results reproducible. Parallelism. default cores = 1 fits replicates sequentially. cores rounds 2 , deterministic per-replicate fits distributed purrr::in_parallel(), uses mirai package backend. boot_pairs() starts cores daemons duration call shuts exit; call relying externally configured mirai daemons. Parallelism speeds computation: never changes numeric result. worthwhile mainly large B large n; small problems setup overhead can dominate. Rank-deficient resamples. resample can rank deficient (example resample omits observations identify coefficient). replicates dropped, warning reports many dropped, summaries use remaining replicates. call errors fewer two valid replicates remain.
